name: HCL Technologies Ltd
title: HCL Technologies Ltd - 532281 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: HCLTech Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2.3% QoQ to $3,724M and EBIT margin hit 18.2%, while FY27 revenue guidance was narrowed to 2.5%-4%.
summary.overview: Services grew 3% QoQ and 4% YoY in constant currency, led by Advanced AI revenue of $219M (up 28.4% QoQ, 78% YoY). New bookings were $3.3B (up 27% YoY, 35% QoQ), the second-highest quarter ever. HCLSoftware revenue fell 5.8% QoQ and 11.2% YoY to $294M, though ARR rose 7.8% YoY to $1.134B (2.6% ex-Jaspersoft). EBIT margin was 18.2%, up 131 bps QoQ, and FY27 EBIT guidance of 17.5%-18.5% was maintained.

financial_highlights.change: +131 bps QoQ, +71 bps YoY; 19.0% adjusted for restructuring (84 bps)
LTM payout INR60, 88.6% of net income
+261 bps YoY; Services 49.4% (+411 bps), Software 19.2% (-264 bps)

segments.name: IT and Business Services (ITBS)
segments.commentary: Grew 2.7% QoQ and 4.4% YoY in constant currency. Growth was broad-based across verticals and geographies.

segments.name: Engineering and R&D Services (ERS)
segments.commentary: Grew 4.1% QoQ and 2.1% YoY in constant currency.

segments.name: HCLSoftware
segments.commentary: Revenue of $294M fell 5.8% QoQ and 11.2% YoY, mainly from fewer multiyear license renewals (multiyear subscription revenue $39M vs $81M in Q2 FY26). ARR grew 7.8% YoY to $1.134B.

guidance_outlook: FY27 company revenue growth (constant currency) guidance narrowed to 2.5%-4%, including 87 bps inorganic contribution; organic midpoint broadly unchanged.
FY27 Services revenue growth guidance 3%-4%, including 62 bps inorganic contribution.
FY27 EBIT margin guidance unchanged at 17.5%-18.5%.
Management expects Services to land slightly above the guidance midpoint; Q3 expected to be strong with a Software step-up.
Mega deal won in the quarter will not contribute revenue in Q3 or Q4; expected to start in Q1 FY28.
Management's desired medium-term EBIT band is 18%-19%, but it declined to commit to this given industry change.
capex_capacity: First AI data center planned in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, in partnership with Sarvam and the Government of Odisha.
Global Technology Center announced in Bhubaneswar; new Global Technology Center opened in GIFT City, Gujarat for financial services clients.
Advanced semiconductor lab launched in Bengaluru with an investment of INR185 crore (post-silicon engineering, testing, validation and failure analysis).
Completed acquisition of HPE's Telco Solutions Group (2 months consolidated in Q2, about $21M revenue); Jaspersoft fully consolidated (about $15M).
Announced intent to acquire Robotiq.ai, a Croatia-based enterprise RPA platform provider.
demand_pricing: Pipeline described as strong and balanced across service lines, verticals and geographies; healthy demand toward end of quarter, but management remains cautious given a fluid environment.
Large AI deals were largely single-sourced through partners; competition came mainly from boutique providers and from service providers in agentic AI build, semiconductors and inferencing.
Management said IP and platform revenue carries gross margins upwards of 70%; AI services margins are at least 7%-10% higher than traditional services.
Top-client buckets: +1 client in $100M+, +8 in $50M+, +10 in $20M+, +33 in $10M+ on a YoY basis. Three top-20 clients ramping down (two telcos, one manufacturer) were already factored into guidance.
Geographic growth YoY: USA +3.5%, Europe -0.3%, Rest of World +11.4%, India +21.8%. Retail and CPG +14% and Financial Services +7.1% led verticals; 5 of 7 verticals grew YoY.

qa_highlights.question: How is value shared between frontier AI labs and managed services, and how will it look in steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its value sits mainly in the FDE motion and services around OpenAI and Anthropic platforms, with a long tail of work once inside an enterprise. Pricing for some offerings includes token cost, making the economics non-linear rather than headcount-linked.

qa_highlights.question: Who is HCLTech competing with in Advanced AI deals?
qa_highlights.answer: The two largest AI deals were single-sourced via partners. Competition came from boutiques, and from service providers in agentic AI build, semiconductors and inferencing; IP platform monetization (e.g., AI Force line items) is now included in large deals.

qa_highlights.question: When will FCF-to-net-income conversion return to the 3-4 year average?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Shiv Walia said two one-time items (a bilateral advance pricing agreement tax payment and a contribution to an external gratuity trust) depressed LTM conversion; he expects it to revert to 100%+ as they roll out of LTM.

qa_highlights.question: Why not raise the top end of guidance given strong Services growth and a seasonally strong Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the environment remains volatile (citing the Middle East conflict) and it does not want to raise guidance; it expects Services slightly above the midpoint and a Q3 Software step-up.

qa_highlights.question: Are the AI engagements with OpenAI/Anthropic under T&M or fixed price, with meaningful TCV?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a mix: change management and operating model transformation engagements have some fixed-price deals, while agentic implementation on Google and similar platforms is largely time-and-materials.

qa_highlights.question: Are the ramp-downs in top-20 clients behind us?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact from the three ramp-downs was already in guidance, though discretionary spend at the two telco clients could still weigh. Upselling to existing clients has kept the client buckets growing.

qa_highlights.question: Why does Software margin expand while revenue declines, and how do Services margins look?
qa_highlights.answer: Software Q1 had a one-off restructuring cost; excluding it, lower employee costs and lower amortization drove the QoQ margin gain. Services margins benefited from Project Ascend and the higher Advanced AI mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organic decline in Software and how long can ARR-to-revenue disconnect last?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue fell about 15% YoY on an organic basis while ARR rose 2.6% ex-Jaspersoft. Management attributed the gap to upfront recognition of multiyear licences and perpetual licence timing, expecting renewals to return in FY28 and FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Is there seasonality in HPE Telco Solutions (Aruba TS) revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only two months were consolidated and extrapolating to three months should be right; there may be small seasonality but nothing major.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q3-Q4 Services sequential growth expected to decelerate versus Q2 organic growth of about 2.4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the mega deal not contributing until Q1 FY28 as the main outlier, and said it is being conservative given uncertainty, with Services likely above the midpoint.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue comes from ecosystem partners, and what is the impact of frontier-lab partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not track partner-channel revenue reliably, much of it is influenced rather than direct. It is a small but growing professional services partner for hyperscalers and frontier and GPU companies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term margin range?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said the earlier aspiration of 18%-19% remains the desired band, but he would not commit to it now, preferring to invest in capability and differentiation.

risks_watch: HCLSoftware: revenue declined 11.2% YoY; the gap to ARR growth depends on multiyear renewals returning in FY28-FY29.
Discretionary spending pressure at two telco top-20 clients, plus a steep budget-driven ramp-down at one manufacturing client.
Free cash flow conversion (LTM FCF to NI 87%) depressed by BAPA tax payment and gratuity trust funding; watch for reversion to 100%+.
Mega deal revenue begins only in Q1 FY28; H2 FY27 Services sequential growth looks slower than Q2.
Macro and geopolitical volatility (Middle East conflict cited) and US PERM program suspension (management says immaterial).
Limited disclosure of partner-channel and AI revenue split; AI pricing and token-cost pass-through economics still evolving.
summary.management_tone: Confident on AI momentum, bookings and margins, but cautious on guidance: management declined to raise the top end, citing a volatile environment. Management was explicit in pushing investors toward ARR rather than reported Software revenue.
key_quotes: I think our value here is largely in the FDE motion, the services around it.
So we should be able to see that this FCI to NI revert to maybe 100% plus level as these one-off roll over from LTM calculation.
Excluding the impact of Jaspersoft, our ARR has grown 2.6% YoY despite a 15% YoY decline in revenue.
But 18% to 19% is our desired band, but I wouldn't want to kind of comment on it now, because the industry is changing significantly
We are seeing a good environment, and we hope it will continue. For Services, we feel confident to be slightly above the midpoint.
